Soc."],"accepted":{"date-parts":[[2023,9,30]]},"published-print":{"date-parts":[[2025,1,27]]},"abstract":"<jats:p>\n                    We construct examples of black hole formation from regular, one-ended asymptotically flat Cauchy data for the Einstein\u2013Maxwell-charged scalar field system in spherical symmetry which are exactly isometric to extremal Reissner\u2013Nordstr\u00f6m after a finite advanced time along the event horizon. Moreover, in each of these examples the apparent horizon of the black hole coincides with that of a Schwarzschild solution at earlier advanced times. In particular, our result can be viewed as a definitive\n                    <jats:italic>disproof<\/jats:italic>\n                    of the \u201cthird law of black hole thermodynamics.\u201d The main step in\u00a0the construction is a novel\n                    <jats:inline-formula>\n                      <jats:tex-math>C^{k}<\/jats:tex-math>\n                    <\/jats:inline-formula>\n                    characteristic gluing procedure, which interpolates between a\u00a0light cone in Minkowski space and a Reissner\u2013Nordstr\u00f6m event horizon with specified charge to mass ratio\u00a0\n                    <jats:inline-formula>\n                      <jats:tex-math>\\frac{e}{M}<\/jats:tex-math>\n                    <\/jats:inline-formula>\n                    . Our setup is inspired by the recent work of Aretakis\u2013Czimek\u2013Rodnianski on perturbative characteristic gluing for the Einstein vacuum equations. However, our construction is fundamentally nonperturbative and is based on a finite collection of scalar field pulses which are modulated by the Borsuk\u2013Ulam theorem.\n
